_meta.note: Data table for bin/route.mjs (the routing bundle). Five grids, all editable without touching code: `cells` keys on (stakes level, role) and yields the model and the two rungs, `review` keys on (level, trigger) and yields a gate, `tiers` and `efforts` key on (level, trigger) and yield the cross-model reviewer's model tier and reasoning effort, `verify` keys on the level alone. Models are Claude dispatch aliases (opus/sonnet/haiku/fable) - stable, not dated ids, so no staleness. Effort is fixed per agent FILE in frontmatter, so varying it means varying the file: a cell's rung names a file, and cadence-core/bin/lib/rung-agent.mjs says which.
_meta.rungs: A rung costs an agent file, and every registered agent's name/description/tools ride in the main session prompt - so the reachable rungs are exactly the ones some cell names, not a rung_order x roles cross product. The rung -> filename map is stated per role in cadence-core/bin/lib/rung-agent.mjs (it cannot be derived: the analyzer's unsuffixed file is its xhigh rung), and self-verify fails in BOTH directions - a cell naming a rung with no file, and a rung file no cell reaches.
_meta.cells: The (stakes level, role) grid: one cell per pair, each yielding the `model` the role runs at, the `effort` rung it starts at and the `retry` rung a failed attempt climbs to. 18 cells, read in one screen - `tier` is gone, and with it the indirection that pinned a role's model to a field named after something else. A `retry` at or above its `effort` is the rule self-verify enforces; equal means the rung is held.
_meta.roles: The declared ARRAY of routable role names, and what route.mjs checks a `--role` against.
_meta.review: The `review` grid keys on (stakes level, trigger name) and yields the gate that trigger fires at, for the four triggers config.schema.json defines. `risk_surface` is deliberately `blocking` at EVERY level: it fires only on a detection match, so there is no level at which a matched risk surface is worth waving through. A `review.triggers.<t>.gate` a user set wins over the level's value and route.mjs reports the disagreement in `warnings`.
_meta.verify: The `verify` grid keys on the stakes level ALONE - the deep-verify pass has no role in hand when it decides whether to run. It is two-state (`off`/`on`); the depth of that pass is carried by the cad-verifier row of the effort grid, not here.
_meta.tiers: The per-trigger model tier the reviewer-availability test uses when NO config layer set `review.triggers.<t>.tier`, keyed on (stakes level, trigger) since RVW-03: raising `stakes` has to move BOTH halves of a panel, and a row keyed on the trigger alone left the cross-model half fixed while the subagent half climbed the cells grid. The ladder runs `tier_names` strongest-first - `critical` names the strongest tier a trigger takes, `shipped` one step down, `solo` one step below that, holding at `cheap` rather than naming anything outside the vocabulary. Transcribed here by hand rather than read from config.schema.json's defaults, for the reason `triggerGatesIn` already states for gates: route.mjs must never turn a schema default into a user assertion. Reading the default would make "the schema says flagship" indistinguishable from "the user asked for flagship", and with the key unset - which is the shipped state, since templates/config.json writes no `triggers` block at all - every provider would resolve unavailable and the fallback reported in `warnings` would be an artifact of the seam rather than the user's config. A config layer that DOES set the key wins over this row.
_meta.efforts: The per-trigger cross-model reasoning effort, keyed the same way as `tiers` and resolved beside it into the same `resolve` envelope (RVW-03). It is the OTHER field that reaches a provider call, so a level that moved the tier alone would leave a raised `stakes` two thirds true. It is not the `effort` of a cell: that one is an agent RUNG naming a file, this one is the `--effort` a cross-model provider request carries, and the two vocabularies are deliberately separate arrays. A config layer that set `review.triggers.<t>.effort` wins over this row, on the same terms as the tier above.
_meta.tier_names: The accepted tier vocabulary, the role `model_aliases` plays for a pin and `gates` plays for a gate: lib/route-cells.mjs checks every `tiers` value against it, in the same file, so the resolver never reads config.schema.json. Declared STRONGEST-FIRST, which is what makes "one step down the ladder" readable off the array.
_meta.effort_names: The accepted cross-model effort vocabulary, playing for `efforts` exactly the role `tier_names` plays for `tiers`, and declared strongest-first for the same reason. Kept beside it rather than folded into `rung_order`: that array is the agent-rung ladder route.mjs dispatches an agent FILE at, and these are the reasoning-effort values a provider request carries - two vocabularies that have never had the same members.
_meta.risk_surface_categories: The eight risk-surface categories `review.triggers.risk_surface.surfaces` is an enum over, and the set route.mjs returns when NO config layer answered. Hand-maintained here for the reason `tiers` and `gates` are: route.mjs must never read config.schema.json, so the resolver needs its own copy of any vocabulary it resolves against. self-verify compares this list, the schema's `values` and the category list in references/review-triggers.md, so the three cannot drift apart.
_meta.gates: The accepted `review.triggers.<t>.gate` vocabulary, checked by route.mjs before a config-set gate may win over the level's gate - the same role model_aliases plays for a pin, in the same file, so the resolver never reads config.schema.json.
_meta.aliases: model_aliases is the accepted vocabulary for a `model.overrides.<role>` pin. The ROUTED vocabulary is narrower - `sonnet` and `opus` - so `haiku` and `fable` are reachable by a pin only. For `fable` that is not a ranking claim: it requires 30-day data retention and returns 400 invalid_request_error for every zero-data-retention org, which is other people's orgs since Cadence ships as a public plugin; its safety classifiers return a refusal stop reason on cyber-adjacent content, and Cadence reviews its own git rails and secrets handling; and its multi-minute turns press against the configured provider request timeout inside the host's Bash ceiling. It is reachable only by explicit pin, which is a user assertion about their own org, not ours.
